papers.title: GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers
papers.abstract: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) contain complementary diagnostic and laboratory information about patient health. However, irregularity, sparsity, heterogeneity, and incompleteness in documentation complicate EHR modeling. To address the problem, we introduce GraphBEAT (Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation over Time), a temporal graph representation learning framework that groups clinical events into time buckets and transforms observed features into patient-specific, temporally directed graphs to enable early risk stratification for gastrointestinal cancers. Each node in an EHR graph encodes feature identity, observed value, and temporal position of clinical events. A context-aware, time-decay message-passing mechanism models transitions between successive buckets, followed by multi-head attention pooling to generate patient-level representations. GraphBEAT was trained and evaluated on multi-site longitudinal diagnosis codes and laboratory tests to predict pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancer at 12-, 24-, and 36-month diagnostic lead times. In all experimental setups, GraphBEAT consistently outperformed baseline graph neural networks (GraphSAGE, GAT, and GCN) and sequence modeling approaches (Transformer and long short-term memory [LSTM]). GraphBEAT also required over 250x fewer floating-point operations per patient and over 20x fewer parameters than the Transformer and LSTM baselines. These results support GraphBEAT as an accurate and computationally efficient approach for cancer risk stratification from sparse, heterogeneous longitudinal health records.

papers.title: BOLT: Universal Classifier Training via a Bayes-Error Upper Bound
papers.abstract: This work introduces a novel approach to compute a universal upper bound on the Bayes error rate (BER) from classifier-output samples, which serves as a Bayes-error-related performance criterion for the underlying classification task. We show that the bound is tight in the binary case and characterize the max-sum gap that appears in the aggregate multiclass formulation. Based on this bound, we define a new loss function, called Bayes optimal learning threshold (BOLT), for training parameterized classifiers. For each data sample, the BOLT loss computes a term whose expectation upper-bounds the Bayes error, so that during training the model parameters can be updated toward minimizing this bound. Numerical experiments with both synthetic and real-world datasets show that, in the reported settings, BOLT training often attains lower held-out classification error than cross-entropy training.

papers.title: Differentially Private Distribution Release of Gaussian Mixture Models via KL-Divergence Minimization
papers.abstract: Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) are widely used statistical models for representing multi-modal data distributions, with numerous applications in data mining, pattern recognition, data simulation, and machine learning. However, recent research has shown that releasing GMM parameters poses significant privacy risks, potentially exposing sensitive information about the underlying data. In this paper, we address the challenge of releasing GMM parameters while ensuring differential privacy (DP) guarantees. Specifically, we focus on the privacy protection of mixture weights, component means, and covariance matrices. We propose to use Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence as a utility metric to assess the accuracy of the released GMM, as it captures the joint impact of noise perturbation on all the model parameters. We develop a KL-divergence-driven optimization framework for differentially private GMM release that jointly designs privacy-budget allocation and parameter perturbations. Through theoretical analysis, we quantify the effects of privacy budget allocation and perturbation statistics on the DP guarantee, and derive a tractable expression for evaluating KL divergence. We formulate and solve an optimization problem to minimize the KL divergence between the released and fitted non-private models, subject to a given $(\epsilon, \delta)$-DP constraint. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves strong privacy guarantees while maintaining high utility.

papers.title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.

papers.title: Tourist arrival forecasting with game-theoretic social influence weighting and deep learning
papers.abstract: In the era of Industry 5.0, data-driven decision-making has become indispensable for planning in service systems such as tourism. This paper proposes a non-linear hybrid approach for forecasting tourist arrivals to Hong Kong from five major source markets before COVID-19 and to Sanya, China, through the COVID-19 shock. The method integrates multiple sources of Internet big data and employs a cooperative game-theoretic algorithm to identify coalitions of opinion leaders on social media, whose content then receives larger weights. The Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT), applied causally, manages nonstationary attributes, and a Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Stacked BiLSTM) network tuned by Bayesian optimization generates the forecasts. We prove that the Shapley values of the underlying trust-weighted coverage game have a closed form and that the coalition of maximal synergy can be found exactly in polynomial time. Relative to the same network fed only with past arrivals, Internet big data reduce the one-step-ahead root mean squared error by 4.1-41.7% across the Hong Kong markets and opinion-leader weighting by a further 10.1-49.4%, against 5.3% and 8.7% for Sanya. The approach compares favorably with published benchmarks and remains robust under volatile conditions, which suggests uses in logistics, supply chains and production planning.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Conditioned RSS-Fingerprint Localization in Cell-Free Millimeter-Wave Networks
papers.abstract: Digital twins (DTs) can generate dense synthetic fingerprints for localization via ray tracing, yet the sim-to-real domain gap limits their direct use, particularly in cell-free millimeter-wave (mmWave) deployments where distributed geometries and blockage-induced sparsity widen the mismatch. We propose DT-conditioned (DTCond), a framework that fuses real and DT beam-domain fingerprints as complementary inputs through per-domain encoders, learnable per-access point (AP) attention, and calibrated uncertainty. We derive oracle and pipeline Cram\'er-Rao bounds (CRBs) for DT-aided fingerprint localization, proving that DT information strictly tightens the positioning bound whenever spatial structure is preserved, with a heteroscedastic refinement that tightens the bound by a further 9.1%. On a real 28 GHz cell-free testbed, the deployable two-stage pipeline, which reads the DT fingerprint at a coarse k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) estimate, achieves 0.284 m mean error against 0.313 m for real-only k-NN. With the DT fingerprint read at the true position (oracle input), DT conditioning achieves 0.186 m mean error, validated through a ten-method ablation against domain-adaptation (DA) and transfer-learning baselines, and a 48% improvement on unseen regions. Multi-user self-attention provides 31-41% per-user gain for emulated simultaneous users, and progressive calibration reduces the measurement budget by 50%. As a use case, localization drives network configuration in closed loop. Between beam sweeps, a DT updated from measured RSS and read at the tracked position estimate selects the 3 of 81 beam pairs that each AP trains. With 49 calibration anchors in the update, the mean beam-selection loss stays below 1 dB over 2 m of motion, whereas reusing the last sweep loses 2.7 dB after 1 m.

papers.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
papers.abstract: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.

papers.title: Orientation-Aware Deep Learning Framework for RSSI-Based Indoor Localization in RIS-Aided mmWave Systems
papers.abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided millimeter wave (mmWave) systems provide directional measurements of received power for indoor localization, but device orientation changes the fingerprints. This work proposes an orientation-aware dual-stream gated (O-DSG) deep learning framework for received signal strength indicator (RSSI)-based indoor localization. An orientation classifier estimates device orientation from RSSI, so inference needs only received power. An embedding of the predicted angle and posterior entropy controls feature modulation and soft expert gating. Parallel convolutional and statistical streams are fused through bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) processing and temporal attention. Single-user measurements in an indoor laboratory at 28 GHz under non-line-of-sight (NLoS) conditions yield a median localization error of 0.141 m, a 25.8% improvement over the closest evaluated baseline (supplied with the measured orientation), and 92.3% orientation classification accuracy across four discrete classes. In spatial regions withheld from training, O-DSG has an average median error of 0.247 m, against 0.392 m for a validation-selected sequence model. A separate offline evaluation constructs non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-style power mixtures from the single-user measurements and measures localization accuracy and computational scaling with up to eight emulated users whose power contributions overlap, under the specified mixture model.

papers.title: Superfast Spectral Compressed Sensing with Quadratic Convergence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the spectral compressed sensing problem of recovering a spectrally sparse signal from linear compressive measurements. Exploiting the low-rank Hankel structure associated with the signal, we formulate a nonconvex fixed-rank optimization problem with a Hankel regularization. We propose a Superfast Iterative Hard Thresholding (SIHT) algorithm, where each iteration consists of a tangent-space least-squares update followed by a fixed-rank hard thresholding projection. SIHT is the first nonconvex algorithm with provable quadratic convergence for spectral compressed sensing. For random Gaussian measurements, it achieves exact recovery in the noiseless case and stable recovery in the noisy case with near-optimal sample complexity. To efficiently implement SIHT, we develop a parameterized conjugate gradient method for solving the least-squares subproblem, endowing SIHT with state-of-the-art computational and memory efficiency. Numerical experiments are provided to validate our results.

papers.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
papers.abstract: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

papers.title: How Does Probabilistic Constellation Shaping Control Ranging Sidelobe Levels in ISAC?
papers.abstract: Probabilistic constellation shaping (PCS), originally designed to fill the gap between finite uniform constellations and continuous capacity-achieving input distributions, has recently emerged as a central tool in adjusting the expected integrated sidelobe level (EISL) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). In this paper, we show that PCS goes beyond EISL: A large class of PCS methods, termed as type-based PCS, are capable of providing precise control over codeword-wise integrated sidelobe level ratio (ISLR) for systems employing orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), thus yielding a stronger sensing performance guarantee than EISL control. We further show that OFDM is almost the only unitary modulation basis whose codeword-wise ISLR can be precisely controlled by type-based PCS. Based upon the analytical results, practical type-based PCS methods compatible with the probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS) framework are conceived, which achieve higher communication rates than existing ISAC-oriented PCS methods under identical ISLR constraints.

papers.title: SNOAR: Self-training with Noise filtering, Observation adding, and Remixing for Speech Denoising Without Clean References
papers.abstract: Unsupervised speech denoising methods such as MixIT and noisy-target training can be trained directly on noisy recordings, avoiding the sim-to-real gap of synthetic training data, but remain well below supervised performance. Teacher--student self-training, as in RemixIT, narrows this gap by remixing a teacher's estimates into new mixtures that supervise a student; however, since the student is trained only toward the teacher's estimates, teacher errors, in particular over-suppressed speech, are never recovered and propagate as the teacher is updated from the student. We propose SNOAR, a self-training framework that corrects the teacher's estimates before use: the noise leaked into its speech estimate is removed by differential noise filtering (DNF), and part of the noisy observation is added back in to restore suppressed speech and attenuate artifacts. We show that the two corrections depend on each other, as without DNF the loop collapses to the identity mapping. Compared to RemixIT, SNOAR is more stable along training and outperforms it in signal-based, perceptual, and word error rate metrics, reaching 97\% of the SI-SDR improvement of a fully-supervised topline on WHAM!; on real CHiME-3 recordings, it improves every metric of three different teachers, while RemixIT degrades their perceptual quality.

papers.title: Cross-subject decoding of imagined speech from scalp EEG: a leakage-controlled evaluation on three public corpora
papers.abstract: Objective. A decoder of imagined speech that works for a new user without calibration would make a non-invasive speech interface practical. We tested whether imagined-speech content recorded with scalp electroencephalography (EEG) transfers across people, and examined why accuracy within a single person remains low. Approach. We analyzed three public corpora, ds003626, KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion and reports exact binomial thresholds, group tests and bootstrap confidence intervals. We trained decoders on each participant and tested them on every other, compared representational geometry across participants without a classifier, applied subject-level alignment, and tested five explanations for the within-subject ceiling. Main results. Across 482 ordered pairs of participants, no pair survived correction for multiple comparisons; mean pair-transfer accuracy lay within 0.006 of chance on every corpus, while every within-subject reference lay above it. Imagery against pre-stimulus rest generalized at about 0.61 after artifact and elapsed-time controls, but its decoder labelled the interval preceding imagery as imagery as often as imagery itself, so the contrast reflects a post-stimulus state, not imagery. Within subject, only the competition corpus decoded above threshold for every participant (0.3147; chance 0.200); syllable count explained little of this, but its frequency profile failed an artifact audit. Significance. In these corpora, imagined-speech content did not transfer between people through any representation we examined. Trial count per class was the only variable that ordered the corpora, which favors larger single-condition datasets over further model development.

papers.title: Antenna Placement for Movable Antenna-Enabled Near-Field Target Localization
papers.abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) have recently emerged as a promising technology to enhance the wireless sensing performance by exploiting additional spatial degrees of freedom. In this work, we consider an MA-enabled near-field target localization problem under a device-based sensing architecture, where the sensing target actively transmits signals and the sensing receiver estimates its location based on the received signals. We adopt the squared position error bound (SPEB) as the sensing performance metric and aim to minimize the target's SPEB by optimizing the antenna placement at the sensing receiver. The resulting optimization problem is highly non-convex due to the minimum antenna spacing constraints and the intricate dependence of the SPEB on the antenna locations and the intractable form of SPEB. To tackle this problem, we first relax the inter-spacing constraints and accordingly formulate an antenna position distribution problem in terms of degree-4 truncated moments. The reformulated moment-based problem admits an equivalent semidefinite programming formulation and can be optimally solved using standard convex optimization solvers. Using truncated moment theory, we then recover an optimal antenna position distribution supported on a finite number of locations and construct an efficient clustered placement policy. Numerical results demonstrate that the constructed optimal distribution exhibits a three-cluster structure with source-dependent weights. The proposed antenna placement method outperforms conventional array geometries and closely approaches the exhaustive-search benchmark scheme.

papers.title: Finite-History Outage Certification for Partially Observed Fluid Antenna Receivers
papers.abstract: Fluid antenna receivers can select a service position from partial port observations, but finite historical data leave uncertainty in the covariance used for that decision. We develop deployment-before-use reliability certification for a frozen partial-observation rule. A proper predictive density defines a history-based parameter region. Gaussian covariance envelopes, shared conditional-probability bounds and selector enclosures provide simultaneous risk bounds over continuous parameters and discontinuous port decisions. Separate history-coverage and integration budgets limit erroneous positive certification to 0.05 for a single qualification procedure under the stated stationary model and numerical assumptions. Confidence-set inclusion allows a new independent history to reuse the risk computation with the rule unchanged. In a structured Gaussian example with 32 candidate positions, five noisy probes and target outage 0.001, all 282 risk groups are qualified; the largest upper bound is 0.000999748. A separate coupled comparison gives a current-rule outage interval of $[7.6820,9.1266]\times10^{-4}$ and resolves lower outage than two observed-port controls using the same historical fit. One independently recalibrated history reuses the certificate without additional risk sampling. Unresolved and adverse-member controls delimit this reuse.

papers.title: Data-driven Smooth-to-hard Spectral Regularization for General Linear Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: The logistic smooth-to-hard shrinker is the proximal map of an explicit saturating spectral penalty for general linear inverse problems. Its exact weak convexity yields a unique scaled update and proximal-gradient stationarity guarantees, while independent validation provides finite-grid parameter-selection control. We use MRI as an illustrative example.

papers.title: Smooth Hard-Thresholding for Singular Values with Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimate
papers.abstract: Low-rank matrix denoising is a central primitive in patch-based image restoration and many other inverse problems. Classical SVD-based image denoising methods often choose a truncation rank by matching residual singular-value energy with an estimated noise energy, but this rule is not a finite-sample risk principle because a fitted low-rank approximation inevitably absorbs part of the noise. This paper develops a mathematically rigorous alternative based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE). Since singular value hard thresholding is discontinuous and does not satisfy the hypotheses of Stein's lemma, we introduce a logistic smooth hard-threshold spectral estimator. We prove that the smooth shrinker satisfies the regularity conditions required by a spectral-estimator version of Stein's lemma, and therefore admits an exactly unbiased fixed-threshold risk estimate under Gaussian noise. For a fixed observed matrix and a finite set of candidate thresholds separated from the observed singular values, the ordering of the fixed-threshold smooth SURE objective eventually agrees with a simple limiting score. The limiting score has the same algebraic form as the biased hard-threshold SURE formula, but here it is used only as a computational device for ranking finite candidates. Selecting the minimizing threshold is a data-adaptive tuning step; the selected SURE value should not be interpreted as an unbiased risk estimate of the finally selected estimator.

papers.title: Event-Triggered Data Selection for Online Frequency-Domain Identification
papers.abstract: Online identification of frequency response functions is increasingly relevant for control and monitoring of high-performance systems whose dynamics may change during operation. In modern machines, however, continuously transmitting all locally acquired measurements to a central unit for identification can impose substantial communication demands, particularly as sensing rates and the number of subsystems increase. This paper develops an event-triggered data-selection approach for remote frequency-domain identification, in which periodically acquired measurements are evaluated locally and transmitted only when relevant. The selection mechanism combines information about the current estimation uncertainty with evidence of model mismatch, reducing communication while preserving identification accuracy and responsiveness to changes in the dynamics.

papers.title: From Signals to Evidence: Interpretable Underwater Acoustic Target Sensing with Large Language Models - Part I: Framework and Recognition
papers.abstract: Underwater acoustic target detection and recognition are essential to marine surveillance and intelligent ocean sensing. Despite substantial advances in deep learning, existing systems typically produce binary detection decisions, categorical labels, or scalar confidence scores, offering limited insight into the physical evidence underlying their outputs. Large language models (LLMs) offer an opportunity to move underwater acoustic sensing toward interpretable, evidence-grounded understanding; however, generic audio encoders struggle to capture the distinctive physical characteristics of underwater acoustics, and physically annotated data are scarce. In this paper, the first of a two-part series, we propose a from-signals-to-evidence framework that integrates physics-aware acoustic encoding with a pretrained LLM, organized around a unified feature-evidence-decision chain with a shared reasoning core. An open input layer accommodates heterogeneous information-raw waveforms, time-frequency representations, environmental and geographic data, and textual physical priors-unifying detection and recognition within a common formulation. In Part I, we instantiate this framework for target recognition through an Underwater Acoustic Physics-aware Transformer (UPT), which tokenizes complementary acoustic representations and learns task-disentangled physical representations through four physics-oriented learning tasks. We develop a physics-parameterized data engine that provides traceable supervision at two levels of granularity and introduce an attribute-level evaluation protocol to assess the physical fidelity of generated descriptions. Experiments on simulated recordings of four vessels demonstrate accurate vessel recognition and reliable estimation of shaft frequency, blade-passing frequency, and machinery-related attributes.

papers.title: A Quad Beam Variable Height Antenna System for Reliable Underground Mine Tunnel Communications
papers.abstract: Mine accidents can damage the wired backbone supporting underground wireless networks, forcing rescue teams to deploy temporary mesh nodes to maintain communication with the surface. Although higher carrier frequencies can support bandwidth-intensive applications such as live video, multimode propagation within mine tunnels produces severe, spatially localized fading. Movable antennas can mitigate these fades by adjusting antenna position; however, moving all antennas on a multi-link relay node simultaneously may improve one link at the expense of another. This paper introduces QuadBeam, a compact mesh node antenna system comprising four independently positionable 2.4~GHz patch antennas mounted on the side faces of a central hub, together with a 900~MHz monopole for backup voice communication. A preliminary prototype incorporates one motor-driven patch mount and three manually adjustable mounts. Bench measurements show interelement coupling below $-46$~dB between patches on adjacent faces. Measurements at five carrier frequencies from 2.40~GHz to 2.48~GHz in the Edgar Experimental Mine reveal 19~dB to 26~dB received-power variations across transmitter and receiver separations of 8.3~m to 18.3~m. Adjusting the receiver height over approximately 20~cm yields received-power improvements of up to 22~dB. Repositioning neighboring patches and removing or reinstalling the monopole produce no noticeable change in the active link. These results demonstrate the potential of independently positioned antennas to alleviate spatial fading in underground mesh communications.

papers.title: A Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Multi-Stream Quickest Change Detection
papers.abstract: A Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework is proposed for quickest change detection (QCD) where there are multiple experts, and each expert produces a sequence of statistics for change detection. A change is declared when a weighted sum of these statistics crosses a threshold. This framework is then applied to the problem of multi-stream QCD to obtain a family of powerful algorithms that outperform the best known algorithms in the literature. In the multi-stream QCD problem, a decision-maker observes multiple streams of observations. At the change point, the distribution of an unknown subset of the streams changes. The optimal algorithm based on a generalized likelihood ratio is computationally expensive. One of the most computationally and performance-efficient algorithms in the literature is the rank-weighted sum (RWS) scheme based on Shiryaev-Roberts statistics. It is shown in the paper that the MoE-based QCD algorithm for multi-stream data outperforms the RWS scheme. This is demonstrated through simulation results on real-valued Gaussian mean shift data and high-dimensional data from Gaussian--Bernoulli Restricted Boltzmann Machines (GB-RBMs).

papers.title: Evolution Toward Sensing-Enabled RAN: Practical Bistatic Sensing via Uplink
papers.abstract: This paper considers uplink channel state information (CSI)-based sensing as an opportunistic approach to enabling sensing in cellular networks, with minimum required modifications to the infrastructure. A practical sensing signal processing procedure is presented, combining 5G positioning function with multi-antenna array processing for passive target localization. The approach is validated through simulation and practical experiments with a software-defined radio-based setup, utilizing open-source software frameworks and commercially available hardware components. Results demonstrate feasibility of the uplink CSI-based sensing for detection, localization and tracking of moving targets over local areas.

papers.title: Resilient and Efficient Aerial Wireless Sensor Networks Using Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a pinching antenna system to enhance the connectivity and efficiency in aerial wireless networks. The algebraic connectivity of the network's graph is maximized by optimizing the placement of the pinching antenna elements in the uplink and downlink waveguides. The number of deployed unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is minimized while maintaining a minimum network connectivity indicator. A heuristic pinching antenna placement algorithm is designed to maximize the network connectivity. An iterative UAV deployment algorithm is also designed to find the minimum number of UAVs, their placement locations, and the pinching antenna placement. Simulation results show that the considered pinching antenna system improves network connectivity and efficiency.

papers.title: Range Ambiguity Identification and Elimination by Leveraging Temporal Broadening Effect for THz Sensing
papers.abstract: High pulse repetition frequency (PRF) operation improves Doppler unambiguous sensing but reduces the maximum unambiguous range of a terahertz (THz) pulsed radar. Echoes from targets beyond this range can be incorrectly associated with subsequent transmitted pulses, causing the targets to appear at shorter ranges. This paper proposes a receiver-side framework that exploits the THz-specific temporal broadening effect as a distance-dependent signature to resolve range ambiguity. For each detected echo, the receiver applies broadening-matched filtering with references corresponding to candidate target ranges. The filter outputs are combined across pulses with Doppler compensation, and the largest normalised combined response identifies the ambiguity order needed to recover the true target range. The selected reference is then reused to reduce mismatch loss in subsequent range and velocity estimation. Simulations under known atmospheric conditions, with targets occupying distinct apparent-delay bins, demonstrate reliable range recovery beyond the conventional unambiguous interval. Range estimation errors conditioned on correct ambiguity-order identification, together with the reported velocity estimation errors, approach their corresponding derived Cram\'er--Rao bounds. The method preserves a fixed transmitted pulse shape, PRF, and sampling rate, at the expense of a higher signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio requirement for ambiguity identification relative to the evaluated diversity-based techniques.

papers.title: How large an effect would we have seen? Positive controls, detection floors and dataset pitfalls in scalp-EEG speech decoding
papers.abstract: Objective. Studies that decode imagined speech from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) commonly validate their pipelines with a positive control, usually overt speech, and report null results without stating what effect size the pipeline could have detected. Approach. Using ds003626 ("Thinking out loud"), KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, we audited decoding of overt speech, articulator preparation and imagined speech with artifact-channel subsets, band-limited decoding and trial selection, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion. We injected class-dependent effects of known amplitude into the real recordings to measure the detection floor of five decoder families, and we checked the ds003626 labels against the dataset's acquisition protocol. Main results. On ds003626, two lip electrodes decoded overt speech at 0.7430 and the eight external channels at 0.7068, against 0.4231 for the 128-channel scalp montage, and no decodable signal survived in the 8-30 Hz band. On the other two corpora, within-subject accuracy rose monotonically with frequency into the range dominated by muscle activity. Band-power logistic regression detected an injected 8-30 Hz desynchronization of 0.54 uV under a criterion fixed in advance, whereas a compact convolutional network (EEGNet) detected nothing within subject up to 4.31 uV. In ds003626, the condition codes are the reverse of the intuitive reading, the class encoding changed between public releases, and condition is a deterministic function of time within each session. Significance. In these corpora the overt-speech positive control is dominated by myogenic signal and cannot validate a decoding pipeline. We recommend that speech-decoding studies report band-limited and artifact-channel accuracy, the direction of accuracy across frequency, and a measured detection floor.

papers.title: Micro-Doppler Sensing for UAV Flight-State Estimation in ISAC Networks
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) provides a promising foundation for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) monitoring. However, most existing studies focus primarily on position and bulk velocity, thus providing limited information about UAV rotor dynamics and orientation. To address this limitation, this paper develops an orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM)-ISAC framework that exploits UAV micro-Doppler signatures to estimate operational states, including rotor rate and rotor-axis orientation, thereby providing richer UAV state information beyond conventional ISAC localization and velocity sensing. The framework progresses from single-station micro-Doppler sensing to multi-station rotor-axis estimation. At each base station, micro-Doppler signatures are first extracted and used to estimate the rotor rate. The framework is then extended to a distributed ISAC network, where view-dependent micro-Doppler signatures from multiple sensing directions are fused to estimate the common rotor-axis direction. Since the fusion relies on Doppler-bandwidth features rather than complex channel phases, inter-station carrier-phase synchronization is not required. We show that three geometrically diverse views can locally identify both the rotor-axis direction and the unknown rotor-tip-speed scale. In addition, a feature-aware radar equation bridges blade radar cross section (RCS), sensing range, transmit power, and observation duration to micro-Doppler detection and rotor-rate estimation accuracy. The effects of residual motion and range migration on the coherent processing interval (CPI) are also analyzed. Simulations and experimental measurements validate the proposed framework and demonstrate the feasibility of rotor-rate estimation and multi-station rotor-axis sensing.

papers.title: Receiver-Specific Interventional Valuation of Semantic Atoms for Budget-Constrained Multi-Agent Communication
papers.abstract: Cooperative multi-agent semantic communication requires deciding not only how a transmitter encodes its observation, but also which resulting semantic content should be delivered to each receiver under a limited link budget. We introduce an encoder-agnostic transmitter-side framework for receiver-specific valuation of independently selectable semantic units, termed semantic atoms. Each atom is assigned a signed value that quantifies whether delivering it is expected to improve or degrade the intended receiver's downstream decision. We formulate this effect through a controlled-delivery utility and identify it via prospective randomized payload delivery before the receiver acts. A shadow receiver estimates this utility using only transmitter-available information, from which receiver-specific leave-one-out (LOO) and Shapley atom values are computed. Experiments on a four-receiver intersection benchmark show 68.4% accuracy in recovering the sign of non-negligible LOO atom effects and a Spearman correlation of 0.302 between estimated and reference LOO values. Under limited budgets, we show that receiver-specific selection consistently outperforms shared and random alternatives, demonstrating the benefit of adapting semantic ranking to the intended receiver. At full affordability, exhaustive subset selection also outperforms full-payload transmission, showing that transmitting all available content need not maximize receiver utility. Overall, our results show that receiver-specific semantic valuation can support effective budget-constrained communication despite imperfect atom-value estimation.

papers.title: Wavefront Engineering for Physical Layer Security in Near-Field Wireless Communications
papers.abstract: With wireless transmission exposing information to potential interception by unintended receivers, physical layer security (PLS) offers a promising approach to securing wireless communications. Beamforming can mitigate this vulnerability by exploiting the spatial characteristics of wireless propagation to concentrate power toward the intended receiver while suppressing it at potential eavesdroppers. However, as wireless systems enter the radiating near field of large-aperture antenna arrays, the resulting wavefront curvature provides additional opportunities for spatial wavefront engineering to enhance PLS. In this work, we investigate the use of different beam types for PLS, including focused, curved, abruptly autofocusing, and cosine beams, generated using uniform linear and planar arrays (ULAs/UPAs). To quantify their performance, we introduce power-based metrics that characterize the power received by the legitimate user and a potential eavesdropper. For all beam types we introduce focusing along the vertical UPA direction, to independently control the phase distributions along the two UPA dimensions and enhance the power discrimination between the legitimate receiver and the eavesdropper. We also propose hollow-focused beams, in which an inactive strip is introduced in the transmitting aperture to create a protected low-power region between the transmitter and the legitimate receiver. The results demonstrate that vertical focusing dramatically enhances the PLS performance and that hollow-focused beams achieve superior PLS performance in both line-of-sight (LoS) and vicinity-of-user (VoU) scenarios.

papers.title: From Interference to Diversity: Mode Coloring and Two-Dimensional Modal-Time Rake Combining for Multipath OAM Communications
papers.abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams provide a spatial-multiplexing dimension for wireless communications, but multipath scattering broadens their mode spectrum, so that energy leaks across modes as inter-mode interference (IMI), which conventional OAM demultiplexing discards. This paper treats the leaked modal energy not as interference but as a structured, harvestable resource: it attains up to $LK$-fold asymptotic diversity under independent-branch fading and yields harvested energy under the rank-limited per-tap fading of the operating channel. Each active OAM mode is colored with a distinct time-domain orthogonal spreading code, and a two-dimensional (2D) receiver grid spanning the OAM modes and the resolvable multipath delays jointly combines the despread outputs. The design builds on the Bessel order-difference coupling law of tilted OAM beams, summarized by a Gaussian mode-diffusion model with a mode-coherence metric that quantifies the surviving orthogonality, and on an effective diversity metric that separates the combining gain available at finite signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) from the asymptotic diversity order. At 28~GHz, with a four-mode eight-element uniform circular array (UCA) and four resolvable multipath taps, the proposed 2D modal-time Rake lowers the bit-error rate (BER) by one to three orders of magnitude and saves roughly 10--15~dB of required SNR over mode-wise detection and mode-domain zero-forcing (ZF) and minimum mean-square error (MMSE) detection, and it also outperforms an uncolored modal-time MMSE equalizer; the advantage survives the spectral-efficiency cost of spreading as well as channel-estimation and timing imperfections.

papers.title: Dual-Purpose SSB Design for Joint Time-Frequency Synchronization Using Relocated DMRS
authors: Sadiq Iqbal (Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
Abdelali Arous (Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
Huseyin Arslan (Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
papers.abstract: The synchronization signal block (SSB) is designed to synchronize a capable user-equipment (UE) with the base-station (BS) in recent cellular networks. However, the same SSB cannot be utilized by a narrowband, low-complexity, and low-power internet of things (IoT) device for synchronization. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a dual-purpose SSB (DP-SSB) to enable low-complexity IoT synchronization using the existing SSB, while ensuring uninterrupted conventional UE operation. Specifically, selected demodulation reference signal (DMRS) symbols are contiguously mapped to some physical resource blocks (PRBs) in the second and fourth symbols of the DP-SSB. These DMRS symbols are further optimized using a receiver-aware least square (LS) approach to impose a distinct time-domain structure at the output of the IoT front-end. At the IoT receiver, a reduced-rate observation of the DP-SSB is obtained after narrowband filtering and decimation that is exploited for energy detection and sequential time-frequency (TF) synchronization. For the UE, primary synchronization signal (PSS) and secondary synchronization signal (SSS)-based synchronization is preserved, while the effect of relocated DMRS on the channel estimation and physical broadcast channel (PBCH) reception is assessed. The performance of the proposed DP-SSB is evaluated in terms of detection probability, TF synchronization accuracy, IoT receiver computational complexity, and UE-side PBCH decoding. Simulation results validate the analytical detection characterization and demonstrate reliable low-power IoT synchronization performance compared with the benchmark synchronization schemes while maintaining conventional UE operation.
